items.title: Quiet Dishes
items.topic: using non-requests as conflict avoidance in shared life
items.angle: If you won’t ask directly, you don’t just avoid a fight-you train the room to keep running on your silence.

items.title: Let-Me-Know Follow-Ups
items.topic: follow-ups that turn into silence
items.angle: If your message avoids the decision, people can’t respond without risking being wrong-so add a deadline and two usable options.

items.title: The Missing Detail
items.topic: Embarrassment dissolves when you name the exact missing thing
items.angle: The threshold doesn’t open for vague apologies-it opens when you offer one usable detail, no bargaining for forgiveness.

items.title: Polite Vagueness Is a Cost
items.topic: Sending the plain request instead of smoothing it into ambiguity
items.angle: You’re allowed to send the sentence you actually mean; the “just checking” edit mostly buys you more waiting.

items.title: Emoji Silence, Live Schedule
items.topic: Emoji reactions replacing real replies in group chats
items.angle: A reaction is a social dodge: it acknowledges presence without taking the small, embarrassing step of committing to the answer.

items.title: Sometime Next Week
items.topic: vague scheduling becoming someone else’s commitment
items.angle: When you dodge a date, you quietly give it away-then you’re stuck negotiating the consequences.

items.title: Affectionate Exit
items.topic: Post-fight texts used to dodge repair
items.angle: An affectionate sign-off after a fight often functions as an off-ramp from accountability, not an arrival to resolution.

items.title: Sure Is a Placeholder
items.topic: When a quick yes is social relief, not commitment
items.angle: The default is “I changed my mind.” The useful frame is “I bargained for comfort, and it got scheduled.”

items.title: Rationing Attention
items.topic: attention as social generosity
items.angle: When your phone pre-books your attention, generosity becomes an exception you keep having to justify.

items.title: Kind Questions, Stuck Room
items.topic: Questions that sound considerate but block the decision
items.angle: When a question can’t be answered without risk, it quietly removes responsibility from the asker-and keeps everyone waiting.

items.title: Brain-Picking Container
items.topic: Setting a time box for vague requests
items.angle: If someone asks to “pick your brain” without a decision or deadline, they’re asking for your attention-so you offer a small, specific container instead.

items.title: The Sentence Before the Sticker
items.topic: Specificity in a time-sensitive handoff beats polite vagueness
items.angle: In public, when the question has a consequence, the kindest move is the exact sentence and the paperwork that matches it.

items.title: Feedback as Permission
items.topic: Using “feedback” to outsource the decision
items.angle: If you call it feedback but you’re really waiting for permission, the delay becomes the point.

items.title: No Rush, Still Due
items.topic: The 'no rush' phrase that quietly schedules you without negotiating time
items.angle: When someone says 'no rush' right next to a deadline, they remove your ability to ask-so you end up doing the prioritizing work for them.

items.title: Whatever, after midnight
items.topic: Misused flexibility that avoids choice but still changes the room.
items.angle: “Whatever” can be a dodge-especially when the decision shows up later as a personal inconvenience.

items.title: Accurate Delivery Beats Apology Polishing
items.topic: Updating an estimate without performing regret
items.angle: You’re allowed to swap the vague apology for a clean new time-because what they’re waiting on is follow-through, not your remorse.

items.title: Let Me Know Isn’t Neutral
items.topic: reframing the phrase “let me know” as a delay tactic
items.angle: “Let me know” can read kind, but it quietly assigns the follow-up to the other person-so the delay becomes the system.

items.title: Quick Thing, Real Cost
items.topic: Work messages that borrow your time
items.angle: The phrase “one quick thing” usually means your calendar is the buffer they’re assuming you’ll provide.

items.title: Scheduling Replies That Offload the Decision
items.topic: Common scheduling phrases that transfer the decision (and stress) onto you
items.angle: When a reply sounds agreeable but avoids specifying a choice, it quietly makes your calendar their fallback plan.

items.title: Owner-by-accident
items.topic: claiming ownership without agreeing to the deliverable
items.angle: If you’re quietly made the owner, you fix it with one written scope-and-deadline sentence before the ambiguity hardens.

items.title: Later as a No
items.topic: Polite deflection that costs you prep time
items.angle: When someone answers with “later,” the exchange reveals they were never agreeing to the work-just buying time.

items.title: Just Checking In Means You’re On Call
items.topic: The social dodge inside “just checking in” after delay
items.angle: “Just checking in” quietly turns your silence into their urgency-then asks you to do the emotional work of fixing it.

items.title: Seen Message
items.topic: attention as a real cost you pay-or refuse
items.angle: When you half-pay attention, you’re not being neutral; you’re choosing what someone’s time becomes.

items.title: Quick Call = Time Borrowing
items.topic: Work messaging and the pressure to drop everything
items.angle: “Quick call” is a request for your availability, not a plan for the work.

items.title: The Disclaimer That Gets You Ignored
items.topic: Meeting pre-apologies and how disclaimers erase your question
items.angle: A “not a dumb question” disclaimer isn’t politeness-it’s permission for the room to dismiss you, and the fix is removing the cushion.

items.title: Name-Repair Rules
items.topic: How to fix a mispronounced name without making the room pay for your embarrassment
items.angle: The cleanest repair is brief correction plus quick return-anything longer turns your mistake into someone else’s job.

items.title: Price in the Invite
items.topic: naming cost before social commitment hardens
items.angle: If a plan costs money, include the number in the invitation so people can answer honestly before politeness gets involved.

items.title: The Wine List Rescue
items.topic: being quietly spared a public class-performance embarrassment
items.angle: The most generous kind of expertise keeps someone in the room without making them display what they do not know.
